steps.say: WORLDLAW finds the rule behind a moving machine from measurements alone. This demo uses a virtual pendulum, so no hardware is needed.
The notebook holds 64 readings of angle, speed, command and torque. Competing explanations are ranked by how well each one fits those readings.
Use suggested state loads the next experiment into the form.
Run the virtual experiment adds one new reading to the notebook.
Next, the feature library. Ask Nemotron opens a request to NVIDIA Nemotron 3 on Nebius Token Factory. The server sends the training readings, not the held-out ones, and keeps the API key.
Nemotron may only name terms from the maintained library. Each proposed term set is fitted by the app itself, on the training readings.
Each proposal shows its equation, its training error, and a held-out check. The held-out check is displayed, but it does not choose the winner.
The explanation the app selected is unchanged. A proposal is a hypothesis until a new reading agrees with it.
That is the loop: measure, compare the explanations, then test again.
